newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A Federal Court ruled yesterday that Victorian power distributor Citipower Ltd must reinstate 125 workers who were stood down eight weeks ago in an industrial dispute. The court issued an interim injunction ordering Citipower to allow three workers to return to work on full pay, despite employee work bans imposed against the company. It is the first time unions have used court injunctions under new industrial legislation against employers. Page 1.

Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer is believed to have ordered an annual salary of A$280,000 be paid to former United Nations Ambassador Richard Butler for two years, following pressure from United States Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and United Kingdom High Commissioner to Australia Roger Carrick. Butler is now head of the United Nations commission in charge of ridding Iraq of weapons of mass destruction. Page 3.

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp yesterday replaced two Labor Civil Aviation Safety Authority board appointees, Gabi Hollows and Geoff Molloy, with aviation experts. The new members are former astronaut Paul Scully-Power and former Royal Australian Air Force wing commander Bruce Byron. Page 5.

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday an upcoming Cabinet meeting to discuss unemployment would not result in any radical new policy measures, despite expectations that the jobless figures would not fall markedly before the end 1997. Howard maintains unemployment will fall as the economy expands and the labour market becomes more flexible. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Fathers groups have called for the abolition of the Family Court and the introduction of joint parenting arrangements following a Full Court decision yesterday allowing a mother to move her daughters 3,200 kilometres away from their father. The court said to stop divorced parents moving could cause financial hardship and was unlikely to be in the best interests of the children. Page 1.

New South Wales Olympics Minister Michael Knight said yesterday all Australians would get a chance to buy tickets to the 2000 Games. A spokesman for Knight said a call by the Liquor, Hospitality and Miscellaneous Workers Union for a ticket lottery for events was a worthy one, and is one of several ideas being considered by the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games. Page 3.

The Department of Defence has warned the Government that without significant increases in defence spending beyond 2000, the military's ability to defend Australia's would be eroded, and put the nation at a higher level of risk. The department claims there is a A$360 million annual shortfall for the planned purchase of Airborne Early Warning and Control aircraft, helicopters for the ANZAC frigates and new offshore patrol vessels. Page 1.

A 59-year-old man who suffered a fractured skull following protests at a meeting of Independent MP Pauline Hanson's One Nation party has called his attackers cowardly and un-Australian. Keith Warburton attended the Dandenong meeting of the party on Monday and was verbally abused by four protesters who broke away from the 1500-strong rally. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Talks were ordered last night by the Industrial Relations Commission for Rio Tinto and the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union. There are fears of a State-wide dispute involving railways developing from a strike over individual work contract or miners at the company's Hunter Valley No.1 mine. Page 1.

Lone Fathers' Association national president Barry Williams has labelled as scandalous a judgement by the Family Court yesterday to uphold a divorced mother's right to move interstate with her daughters. Williams said the decision would cause violence, and that judges would have blood on their hands. Page 1.

Uniting Church national director of mission Reverend Dorothy McRae-McMahon has told an assembly meeting in Perth this week that she is a lesbian, and her ordination would be in question if they voted against a proposal for openly homosexual clergy. The assembly will vote on its report Uniting Faith and Sexuality today. Page 1.

Sydney's Cambodian People's Party president Sambath Va said yesterday he and other Hun Sen supporters in Australia would return to Cambodia if the situation worsened, and could be join the fighting. Va and Australian branch of Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party president Sokhom Pech were yesterday trying to gather support for their opposing sides from the 10,000 Cambodians living in New South Wales. Page 1.
THE AGE

A landmark Family Court case that tested the Federal Government's new custody rights laws ruled yesterday against an appeal by a man seeking to prevent his former wife moving interstate with their children. The case was also seen as a test of the Constitutional right to freedom of movement. Page 1.

State police ministers will meet next week to consider a Federal Government proposal to give doctors, nurses and psychologists legal protection to report people they believe are unfit to own or use a firearm. Victoria and South Australian are trying to soften the proposed changes to gun laws, seeking the removal of the "cooling-off" period for gun owners wanting to buy a second gun. Page 1.

Acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone says convicted American hijacker and former Black Panther group member Lorenzo Ervin had entered Australia by using a different middle name after the Immigration Department's computer data-matching system did not recognise Ervin's "stage-name" of Kom'boa. Ervin will be deported to America tomorrow, despite the validity of his visa being challenged by his lawyers. Page 3.

The Western Mining Corporation has admitted in its latest environmental report that inadequate warning signs and fencing meant a trial uranium mine at Yeelirrie in Western Australia, containing drums of contaminated laboratory products and processed uranium ore, was left exposed to the public for 10 years. The company said the contents of some of the drums had been exposed due to weathering. Page 1.
